name: Battle of Zama
intro: Near Zama, North Africa. You command about 29,000 infantry (hastati, principes, triarii), 6,000 Roman and Italian cavalry, plus Masinissa’s Numidian cavalry. Hannibal fields roughly 40,000 men, 80 war elephants, and a weaker cavalry arm. His veterans wait in a third line behind his levies.
debrief: In reality, Scipio’s lanes let the elephants run through, his cavalry drove off Hannibal’s cavalry, the hastati beat the levies, and the principes and triarii extended the line to face the veterans. Masinissa and Laelius returned from pursuit and struck the rear, ending the battle. Carthage lost perhaps 20,000 killed and as many captured, and the Second Punic War ended. Numbers and details vary by source.

win: The Numidian cavalry thunders into the rear of Hannibal’s veterans.
Caught between spear and hoof, the old soldiers of Italy fall.
The Carthaginian army has ceased to exist.
lose: Your cavalry crashes in, but too little, too late.
Hannibal’s veterans bend but do not break.
Night falls on a field that is still Carthage’s.

options.text: Met Hannibal and refused his terms
Partly broken, your line is ragged
Enemy cavalry routed, yours is away
Raiding too early, enemy cavalry intact

default.text: Held back as Hannibal’s last line

decisions.title: Hannibal asks to talk
decisions.text: Before the armies close, Hannibal sends word that he wants a meeting between the lines. Your men are watching. Hannibal’s army is still settling into its ground.

hint.text: Hannibal will offer terms that leave Carthage with its empire. Rome has been cheated by a truce before.

scout.text: Your scouts report the Carthaginian line is still dressing its ranks. Hannibal is offering terms that keep much of what Carthage holds. Terms that Rome would accept have not been put on the table.

choices.label: Meet him between the armies, hear his terms and refuse them

fx.text: The two generals talk face to face and part with nothing agreed. Your men see their general stand firm, and the Carthaginians see theirs come back empty-handed.

choices.label: Refuse to meet

fx.text: No meeting takes place. Neither army learns anything, and Hannibal’s men have a little more time to settle.

choices.label: Accept his terms and call off the battle

fx.text: You accept. Your men feel cheated of a victory and the Senate is angry. Carthage takes heart, and the battle goes ahead on worse terms.

decisions.title: The elephants
decisions.text: Eighty elephants stand before Hannibal’s line. They will charge first.

hint.text: Prisoners say the elephants were trained for the march, not for javelins. Panicked beasts run for open ground.

scout.text: The elephants have no infantry screening them. Javelins from the side make them turn and bolt. They will crush a solid line in front of them, but they follow open lanes.

choices.label: Open lanes between maniples; velites screen, then fall back

fx.text: The beasts veer or rush down the empty lanes, panicked by horns and javelins. Your line bends but holds.

choices.label: Close ranks into a solid wall

fx.text: The elephants smash into the shields and trample men. Gaps open in your first line.

choices.label: Charge before the elephants are set

fx.text: Some beasts are caught off balance, but your charge is ragged and exposed.

decisions.title: The cavalry
decisions.text: Your cavalry faces Hannibal’s cavalry on both wings. Masinissa’s Numidians are eager.

hint.text: Hannibal’s cavalry is poorly drilled and has orders to hold the wings.

scout.text: Their cavalry is weaker than yours, and the Numidians on their side are wavering. A hard charge should break it. Cavalry that rides off in pursuit is out of position later unless you recall it.

choices.label: Both wings charge and drive the enemy cavalry off the field

fx.text: The Carthaginian cavalry breaks and flees, your cavalry in pursuit. The infantry will fight alone for now.

choices.label: Hold the cavalry back to guard your flanks

fx.text: Safe, but Hannibal’s cavalry stays in play and keeps probing your flanks.

choices.label: Send cavalry around to strike the enemy rear now

fx.text: A bold ride, but the enemy line is still intact and your cavalry arrives too early.

decisions.title: The first line
decisions.text: Hannibal’s mercenaries and levies advance. Your hastati meet them.

hint.text: The first Punic line is mercenaries and levies. Their veterans stand back, uncommitted.

scout.text: Their first line is meant to wear you down, not to win. If you commit your second and third lines too soon, you will have nothing fresh left for the veterans behind them.

choices.label: Hastati advance; principes and triarii stay in reserve

fx.text: The hastati grind forward. Your second and third lines stay fresh.

choices.label: Hastati advance with principes close behind

fx.text: A steady push, but your reserves are committed early.

choices.label: Throw all lines in at once

fx.text: A brutal melee. You hit hard but have nothing left in hand.

decisions.title: A pause to re-form
decisions.text: The fight pauses. Pila are spent, men are thirsty, and wounded clog the front.

hint.text: Your front is thinning. Spent javelins and wounded are clustering in the first ranks.

scout.text: The first line is nearly out of pila and the wounded are blocking the way. Rotating fresh maniples forward is worth the pause. Hannibal is reforming his veterans in the gap.

choices.label: Rotate fresh maniples forward and reissue pila from the baggage

fx.text: Order is restored. The men are ready for the next push.

choices.label: Press on with no pause

fx.text: The pressure holds, but your men tire.

choices.label: Pull back to regroup

fx.text: You rest, but Hannibal uses the time to reform his veterans.

decisions.title: Hannibal’s veterans
decisions.text: The levies are broken. Hannibal’s veterans stand fresh and unbroken in the third line, spears levelled.

hint.text: Hannibal’s veterans form a shorter line than yours.
Hannibal’s veterans form a shorter line than yours. Your reserves are committed, so overlapping them may not be possible.

scout.text: Their line is shorter than yours. Your fresh principes and triarii can swing out and wrap both ends. A frontal clash would be costly.
Your reserves are spent, so you cannot wrap the veterans. A frontal clash would be costly, and waiting gives their cavalry time. Their cavalry is still on your flank.
Your reserves are spent, so you cannot wrap the veterans. A frontal clash would be costly, and waiting gives their cavalry time.

choices.label: Principes and triarii extend to both flanks; one long front

fx.text: Your fresh reserves swing out and overlap the veterans’ front. Hannibal’s men are pinned.
You try to extend, but your reserves are already spent. The line is thin.

choices.label: Frontal assault on the veterans

fx.text: The veterans are Hannibal’s best. The assault costs you dearly.

choices.label: Halt and let them come to you

fx.text: Their cavalry harasses your flank while you wait.
A cautious pause that wins little.

decisions.title: The cavalry returns
decisions.text: Your cavalry has finished the pursuit. Decide where they go.

hint.text: Your cavalry is reforming behind the enemy line.
Your cavalry is scattered and will be late.
Your cavalry is still on the flanks.

scout.text: Laelius and Masinissa have finished the pursuit and are in position. Recalled at once, they strike the veterans’ rear.
Your cavalry rode too early and scattered. It will arrive late if recalled.
Your cavalry never left the flanks, so there is no cavalry behind the enemy to close the circle.

choices.label: Recall all cavalry to charge the veterans’ rear

fx.text: The cavalry thunders in behind the veterans. The trap closes.
Your cavalry is scattered and arrives late, but it still strikes.
Your cavalry never left the flanks. There is no one to close the circle.

choices.label: Let them chase the fleeing cavalry and destroy it

fx.text: The pursuit costs you the decisive moment.

choices.label: Recall half, keep half in pursuit

fx.text: A partial blow. The veterans bend but do not break.
